artists.biography:
Matthew Charles "Matt" Berry (born 2 May 1974) is an English actor, writer, comedian and musician. Berry is perhaps best known for his appearances in The IT Crowd, Garth Marenghi's Darkplace, The Mighty Boosh, and Snuff Box. He is renowned for his deep voice; he has voiced several advertisements, most notably for Volvic, The Natural Confectionery Company, Absolute Radio, and MoneySupermarket.

As a musician, Berry composed all the music for Snuff Box, as well as the music for AD/BC: A Rock Opera, which he co-wrote with Richard Ayoade. AD/BC was a half-hour parody of overblown musicals in general and Jesus Christ Superstar in particular, telling the story of the innkeeper who allowed Mary, Joseph, and the baby Jesus to sleep in his manger. AD/BC was broadcast in December 2004 and featured Fulcher and Mighty Boosh stars Julian Barratt and Noel Fielding. He also performed a song for an episode of Garth Marenghi's Darkplace entitled "One Track Lover", a spoof of cheesy romantic 80s songs.

perplexity.description:
Top Brass" by Matt Berry, originally released in 2023 on Acid Jazz, is an instrumental album that blends elements of electronic, rock, and classical music. The album features lush orchestral arrangements, vintage synthesizers, and a strong jazz influence, reflecting Berry's background in both television composition and rock songwriting. The title track, "Top Brass," is a standout, showcasing his flair for dramatic melodies and cinematic textures, while the "Bare Essentials Mix" offers a stripped-down, more intimate take on the same material. The album's sound is both retro and contemporary, drawing on classic library music and 1970s British TV scores while maintaining a modern production sensibility.

Within Matt Berry's discography, "Top Brass" represents a focused exploration of instrumental composition, distinct from his more vocal-driven rock and pop albums. It follows his established reputation for crafting evocative, genre-blending music, particularly through his work on television soundtracks. The album was well-received for its craftsmanship and nostalgic yet fresh approach, with critics praising its sophisticated arrangements and Berry's ability to merge disparate musical styles into a cohesive whole. Its release on Acid Jazz, a label known for its eclectic and jazz-influenced catalog, further underscores its place within a tradition of innovative British instrumental music.
